introduction: On this most holy night, the Church keeps vigil for the Lord's Resurrection. We begin in darkness, with the new fire and the Easter candle, the sign of Christ our light. We listen to the story of salvation, from creation to the promises of the prophets. Tonight catechumens are baptized and receive the sacraments, and we all renew our baptismal promises. With the women at the tomb, we hear: He is not here; he has been raised.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, on this night of light we rejoice with the newly baptized. Let us pray to the Father, who raised his Son from the dead.
intentions: For the Church throughout the world, keeping vigil tonight: that the light of the risen Christ may shine through her in every land. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the newly baptized and all who have been received into full communion: that they may walk in newness of life. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who live in fear: that the risen Lord may say to them, Do not be afraid. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have died, especially those we have loved: that they may share in the Resurrection of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves, who have renewed our baptismal promises: that we may live as people who are dead to sin and alive to God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of life, on this night you raised your Son from the dead and gave new life to your children in Baptism. Keep us faithful to the promises we have made, and fill us with Easter joy. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Do not be afraid
reflection.body:
The Easter Vigil tells the whole story of salvation in one night. We hear how God created everything and "saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good." We hear Abraham's trust: "God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son." We hear how Israel walked through the sea on dry ground. And we hear the prophets' promise of a new heart and a new spirit.

All of this leads to the font. Paul explains what Baptism does: "We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life."

Matthew's Gospel takes us to the tomb at dawn. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary come to see the tomb. There is an earthquake, and an angel rolls back the stone and sits on it. The guards are so terrified that they "became like dead men." The angel speaks to the women: "Don't be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said."

The women run from the tomb "with fear and great joy." And on the way, Jesus himself meets them: "Rejoice!" They take hold of his feet and worship him. He tells them, "Don't be afraid. Go tell my brothers that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me." The first witnesses of the Resurrection are sent as messengers to the apostles.

The angel and Jesus both say the same words: do not be afraid. Tonight, as you renew your baptismal promises and receive the light of the Easter candle, hear those words spoken to you. Christ is risen. Go and tell others.
